speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these cough and shortness of breath symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I've been dealing with this persistent, dry cough and feeling winded for about three months now. The shortness of breath gets worse whenever I try to do physical activities like playing basketball. However, hospital policy during the current surge is to avoid non-essential labs. Cardiac diagnosis must be made from clinical evaluation only.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the hospital's restrictions; let's focus on your physical exam. On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate the severity of your shortness of breath when you are at rest?

speaker: Patient
text: It's pretty mild at rest, maybe a 2 or 3 out of 10. But as soon as I start walking briskly or climb stairs, it jumps up to around a 6 or 7. I want to emphasize that, hospital policy during the current surge is to avoid non-essential labs. Cardiac diagnosis must be made from clinical evaluation only.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the need to rely on clinical evaluation. Does your cough produce any sputum, and if so, what color is it?

speaker: Patient
text: No, the cough is completely dry and I don't produce any sputum at all. I also haven't noticed any blood in my mouth or any changes in my weight recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness when you exert yourself? Also, have you noticed any swelling in your legs or ankles lately?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't get any chest pain, dizziness, or heart racing when I push myself. My legs and ankles have been completely free of any swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your symptoms are exertional and you have no swelling or chest pain, are you experiencing any orthopnea (shortness of breath when lying flat) or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (waking up gasping for air)?

Do you have a history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or are you currently taking any medications?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't wake up gasping for air or feel short of breath when I lie down flat. Regarding medications, I haven't been prescribed any new drugs recently, though I do have a history of high blood pressure.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful; given your history of hypertension and the exertional nature of your symptoms, do you have any history of smoking, and have you noticed any recent weight loss or loss of appetite?

REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram (M-mode/2D)
REQUEST TEST: ECG (Electrocardiogram)

DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypertensive Heart Disease with Left Ventricular Hypertrophy leading to Exertional Dyspnea
